name: Malai Ki Gilori
instructions: 1. Collect fresh malai sheets (cream) from boiled milk and let them drain on muslin cloth.
2. Prepare the stuffing by sautéing khoya with sugar, cardamom powder, and chopped nuts until firm.
3. Cut the delicate malai sheets into squares or triangles.
4. Place a small portion of the khoya mixture onto the malai piece.
5. Carefully fold the malai sheet into a triangular shape to resemble a 'paan' (betel leaf) or gilori.
6. Garnish with edible silver leaf (vark) and chill before serving.
description: Originating from the royal kitchens of Lucknow, Malai Ki Gilori is a sophisticated delicacy that mimics the shape of the traditional Paan. It is highly esteemed in Awadhi cuisine for its velvety texture and is a hallmark of the refined dessert culture of Uttar Pradesh.
